title: Excellence of strict local rings of finite-type field algebras
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $B$ a finitely generated commutative $k$-algebra (a quotient of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables). Let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal of $B$, put $L=B_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], choose a separable closure $K$ of its residue field, and let $C=L^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be a strict henselization relative to $K$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Then $L$, $C$, and every quotient $C/I$ by an ideal $I$ are excellent. In particular $C$ and $C/\sqrt{(0)}$ are Noetherian.

Here a ring $D$ is excellent if it is a Noetherian G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], its regular locus is open after every finite-type algebra extension, and it is universally catenary. More explicitly, for every finitely generated $D$-algebra $E$, the subset of $\operatorname{Spec}E$ consisting of primes $\mathfrak q$ for which $E_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] is open, and for any two primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak r$ of $E$ all saturated chains of primes between them have the same finite length; a chain is saturated if no additional prime can be inserted between successive terms. The ideal $\sqrt{(0)}$ consists of the nilpotent elements of $C$.
